codex.rollback: supported - fault injection after the entrypoint stage commits, full rollback; test_codex_adapter.py scenario 17

codex.adapter_switching: supported for both claude-code<->codex (scenarios 3-5, 18a/18b) and cursor<->codex (scenarios 27-30), both directions. Unlike Cursor (full-regen), switching away from codex or claude-code strips the EIF block but does not delete the file, since a marker-merge entrypoint's placeholder footer is never empty - verified explicitly in scenario 4. Switching AWAY from codex reads its actual prior entrypoint from the lock (not the static greenfield default), since the prior write may have gone to AGENTS.override.md rather than AGENTS.md.
codex.runtime_consumption_evidence: CONFIRMED for the CLI surface (Codex Cloud's global scope is not independently verified - it keeps its own separate environment/workspace configuration per the official docs, though the project-scope AGENTS.md content EIF manages is part of the repo itself and should behave identically there). Verified 2026-07-17 against `codex --version` (codex-cli 0.144.5) and the official docs, re-fetched during the active-entrypoint correctness round to confirm project_doc_fallback_filenames. A 2026-07-18 post-merge review found the first-pass description of project-root discovery and the size budget had never been checked against Codex's own PRIMARY source (only the secondary docs page) and was wrong on both: root discovery does not walk to the filesystem root when no `project_root_markers` marker exists anywhere (it inspects cwd alone), and `project_doc_max_bytes` truncates a file mid-content rather than skipping it whole - both fixed and re-verified against `github.com/openai/codex` commit `3a067484584861606ad842de5bc4ac735a865ddf`. Real runtime proof via `codex debug prompt-input` (no authentication required), repeated from the INSTALLED WHEEL (`eifctl init --adapter codex`) against disposable probe projects, including one run entirely against an isolated, empty `CODEX_HOME` (2026-07-18): confirmed the actual wheel-generated AGENTS.md is loaded; confirmed a same-directory AGENTS.override.md becomes the active target exactly as eif_verify_runtime.py's doctor predicts; confirmed a nested subdirectory's own AGENTS.md is appended after the root's content when cwd is inside it; confirmed a 40000-byte decoy parent AGENTS.md is never read when no root marker exists anywhere; confirmed the real truncation point at a lowered project_doc_max_bytes matches this adapter's own simulator byte-for-byte. See adapters/codex/README.md for the full evidence trail (sanitized - no raw probe output retained anywhere, any round).

hermes.entrypoint: entry_strategy=dynamic-resolve via resolve_hermes_active_source() (NOT resolve_active_entrypoint() - Hermes's real precedence needs an ancestor walk for tier 1 evaluated before tiers 2-4 are even considered at the instance root). Four real tiers, first match wins: (1) .hermes.md/HERMES.md, nearest ancestor from cwd to the git root, no depth cap; (2) AGENTS.md/agents.md, instance root only; (3) CLAUDE.md/claude.md, instance root only; (4) .cursorrules + .cursor/rules/*.mdc, instance root only, never a marker-merge target. Supersedes closed, unmerged PR #12, whose own implementation and evidence are not reused - see adapters/hermes/README.md 'What PR #12 got wrong'.

hermes.adapter_switching: supported for claude-code<->hermes, both directions (scenarios 3/4). A real, pre-existing defect in the generic adapter-switching transaction (not specific to Hermes's own contract) was found and fixed while building this adapter: CLAUDE.md is both claude-code's fixed entrypoint AND one of Hermes's own tier-3 candidates, so a same-path switch previously double-staged the same '<path>.next' file for two separate transaction stages and crashed with 'staged artifact missing' - see adapters/hermes/README.md for the full root cause and fix.
hermes.runtime_consumption_evidence: CONFIRMED for the local CLI surface (Hermes Cloud/gateway/mobile surfaces not independently verified). Verified 2026-07-18 directly against the installed Hermes Agent's own Python source (a git install, not a black-box wheel) - see adapters/hermes/README.md for the full primary-source evidence trail, including several concrete errors found in closed PR #12's own 'verified' claims (a fabricated 5-level ancestor cap, missing lowercase filename fallbacks, an unmodeled Cursor-format 4th tier, and a completely wrong truncation model). Real runtime proof via `hermes prompt-size --json` (offline, no API call), from an isolated, freshly-created `HERMES_HOME`, repeated from the INSTALLED WHEEL (`eifctl init --adapter hermes`): confirmed the real CLI, run from a cwd 7 directory levels below the probe project root, still finds the ancestor .hermes.md (no depth cap, directly contradicting PR #12's claim); confirmed the real CLI's own truncation warning reports the exact same source character count (4104) that this adapter's own simulator independently computed for the identical file at the identical configured limit. Also includes a real, pinned-version proof against the actual installed Hermes security scanner (not vendored) that EIF's generated EN/UK content is never blocked, plus a control fixture proving the check can detect a real block. See adapters/hermes/README.md 'Runtime-validation status' for the full trail (sanitized - no raw probe output retained anywhere).
